h1: Utility land clearing for pipeline, powerline and waterline work
lede: 9 Arrow Land Service provides utility land clearing in Texas for gas pipelines, powerline corridors and waterlines. We open the easement, clear to survey data, build access and come back to keep the right-of-way open.

answer.q: Who provides utility land clearing in Texas for pipelines and powerlines?
answer.a: 9 Arrow Land Service provides utility land clearing in Texas for utility companies, service providers and field contractors. The Spring Branch crew clears gas pipeline, powerline and waterline corridors, typically 30 to 120 feet wide, integrates survey data into the clearing, builds access roads and pad sites, and returns for ongoing right-of-way maintenance.

highlights: Often first contractor on the easement
Survey data built into the clearing

sections.h2: Utility land clearing ahead of construction crews
paras: Utility projects stall when the easement is still standing timber. 9 Arrow is often the first contractor on site, opening the easement ahead of grading crews, dozers and excavators. Our [right-of-way clearing](right-of-way-clearing) crews clear gas pipeline, powerline and waterline corridors, typically 30 to 120 feet wide and often 90 feet or more, on routes that can run for many miles.

9 Arrow mulches the corridor where it stands, so there are no burn piles to manage and no debris to haul off the easement. Our compact track machines work slopes, tight access and uneven ground, and our large articulated wheel machines bring high horsepower and high production.

sections.h2: Utility easements and pad sites cut to survey data
paras: 9 Arrow mounts Trimble data collectors and receivers on our mulchers and loads the licensed surveyor's CAD files, so our operators follow certified survey data with real-time GPS guidance. Our [survey line clearing](precision-line-survey-clearing) covers utility rights-of-way, easements and pad sites for oilfield and utility projects, and it reduces or eliminates survey-crew pre-staking. 9 Arrow is not a licensed surveyor and does not replace one.

Utility crews need roads that carry heavy equipment and truck traffic. 9 Arrow handles [access road building](roads-and-access-preparation) with clearing, rough and fine grading, culverts, drainage and erosion control, and we can crush surface rock on site into road base instead of importing material. We grade each road with proper crown and drainage so it stays usable through changing weather.

sections.h2: Right-of-way maintenance and safety for utility partners
paras: Cleared corridors grow back, and mesquite regrowth is aggressive. 9 Arrow maintains rights-of-way with tractor and batwing equipment, and our [grounds maintenance](grounds-maintenance) crews handle gas pipeline ROW maintenance, signage clearing and access-corridor upkeep.

9 Arrow keeps a written [electrical right-of-way safety manual](electrical-right-of-way-row-safety-manual-texas) for electrical ROW work. The manual page outlines what the manual covers and how to get a copy.

faqs.q: How wide are the utility corridors 9 Arrow clears?
faqs.a: Utility corridors that 9 Arrow clears are typically 30 to 120 feet wide, and often 90 feet or more. Routes for gas pipelines, powerlines and waterlines can run for many miles. 9 Arrow is often the first contractor on site, opening the easement ahead of grading crews, dozers and excavators.

faqs.q: Does 9 Arrow maintain utility rights-of-way after clearing?
faqs.a: Yes. 9 Arrow provides ongoing right-of-way maintenance with tractor and batwing equipment, which keeps aggressive regrowth such as mesquite in check. Our grounds crews also handle gas pipeline ROW maintenance, signage clearing and access-corridor upkeep, so the corridor stays open long after the initial clearing.

faqs.q: How is utility land clearing priced?
faqs.a: 9 Arrow prices utility land clearing after a discovery call, a site visit or both. The estimate depends on vegetation density, tree size and species, topography, access, maneuverability and soil conditions along the corridor. We show the estimate by the day or by the acre, and survey data helps define the scope.

faqs.q: Does 9 Arrow have a safety manual for electrical ROW work?
faqs.a: Yes. 9 Arrow keeps a written Electrical Right-of-Way (ROW) Safety Manual for utility clearing work. The safety manual page on this site summarizes what the manual covers. Utility partners who want a copy can call (210) 247-8410 or email john@9arrow.com to request one.
